source.title: Rethinking generalization of classifiers in separable classes scenarios and over-parameterized regimes
source.authors: Julius Martinetz; C. Linse; T. Martinetz

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper and appendix; no garbling or cutoff is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: Reports experiments on held-out error for over-parameterized classifiers across model sizes and architectures, using different settings and measures from the claim versions’ cited studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports natural-label training and test results, but does not run random-label controls, a width sweep of one-hidden-layer ReLU networks, or optimizer, batch-size, regularization, sharpness, or memorized-example interventions. Table 1 reports fitted learning-curve parameters; test-error curves are shown in figures.
record.test_reason: The study tests V3 by comparing held-out CIFAR-10 errors of convolutional ResNets and fully connected MLPs trained from scratch with LAMB. Its depth and parameter-count comparisons do not test V2's width intervention, and natural-label fits without random-label experiments do not test V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors derive an exponentially decreasing bound on the fraction of bad zero-training-error solutions for separable classes and extend their density-of-classifiers account to overparameterized classifiers using an approximation and a uniform-selection assumption. Their fitted learning curves broadly match MNIST and CIFAR-10 experiments. Larger ResNets have lower fitted minimum errors and faster convergence with sample count; the faster-convergence trend does not hold for the deeper MLP.
record.recipe_differences: Uses LAMB, no weight decay, and zero-training-error fits across training-set sizes; the claim versions concern different interventions and comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and architecture change the fitted Emin and learning-curve scaling factor η; the paper reports that larger ResNets converge faster, while the larger MLP converges more slowly.

fits_no_version.finding: Natural-label networks achieve zero training error while generalizing above chance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overparameterized classifiers can interpolate natural-label training data and still generalize; this does not establish coexistence with random-label memorization under the same recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger ResNets have lower fitted minimum error and require fewer samples to approach it; the deeper MLP has a slightly lower fitted minimum but a larger sample-scaling factor.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing depth and parameter count can improve generalization, with architecture-dependent sample requirements.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Network (Version of Record presented at 2024 IJCNN)
record.problems: The over-parameterized experiments assume zero training error and compare fitted learning-curve parameters; exact test-error values are presented in figures. Results use 50 runs per setting, with standard deviations shown, but no uncertainty values are stated numerically in the text. Architecture comparisons do not isolate a single architectural feature or size dimension.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows retained. Figure 4 and Figure 5 show separate test-error points over many training-sample counts, but the supplied text does not give their numerical values; Table 1 provides fitted parameters for the model/dataset sweeps.

untested.parts: No fixed random-label training experiments or corresponding held-out controls; the random-label example is cited and modeled.
No width sweep, interpolation threshold, or comparison of widths beyond that threshold. The MLP comparison varies depth.
Local connectivity's causal contribution, learned sparse local connections, convolutional initialization of fully connected networks, and architecture comparisons on MNIST, CIFAR-100, and SVHN.
No optimizer comparison or tuning-budget intervention.
No controlled batch-size comparison at fixed epochs or test of recipe adaptations.
No dropout intervention or joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurements or ranking of generalization measures.
No memorization-based example removal and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V3. R6 and R8 duplicate comparisons rather than supplying independent evidence. Model-fit deviations at small sample counts qualify the density model, not by themselves V3. Figures 4 and 5 are already declared in rows_left_out, so their untranscribed points are not listed as missing.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on random labels or report held-out accuracy for random-label models; the random-label discussion cites Zhang et al. (2017).
Does not sweep width within a fixed one-hidden-layer ReLU architecture, identify the width needed for zero training error, or test downsampled CIFAR-10.

Only compares ResNets with fully connected MLPs on CIFAR-10; does not report MNIST, CIFAR-100, or SVHN architecture comparisons, sparse learned local connections, or convolutional initialization of a fully connected network.
No controlled large-versus-small batch comparison at a fixed epoch budget.
No sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.

rows.subject: ResNet018
rows.operation_detail: Trained on varying numbers of natural-label MNIST examples, to zero training error; reported fitted learning-curve parameters.
rows.note: The paper reports held-out test-error curves in Figure 4, but Table 1 gives fitted Emin rather than a direct test-error value for a specified training-sample count.
rows.check: The value is a fitted asymptotic error parameter, not a measured error at a specified sample count. Natural-label performance alone does not establish V1.

rows.subject: ResNet101
rows.operation_detail: Compared with ResNet018 after training on varying numbers of natural-label MNIST examples, to zero training error.
rows.note: The authors state ResNet101 generalizes better at fixed n and converges faster, despite four times as many parameters. This is a different architecture and depth as well as size, and does not isolate width.
rows.check: ResNet018 versus ResNet101 changes depth and block structure, rather than sweeping width past an interpolation threshold. The fitted values do not test V2.

rows.subject: MLP3
rows.operation_detail: Trained on varying numbers of natural-label CIFAR-10 examples, to zero training error; reported fitted learning-curve parameters.
rows.note: The paper reports held-out test-error curves in Figure 5, but Table 1 gives fitted Emin rather than a direct test-error value for a specified training-sample count.
rows.check: The value is a fitted asymptotic error parameter. This standalone natural-label result does not test V1 or V2.

rows.subject: MLP8
rows.operation_detail: Compared with MLP3 after training on varying numbers of natural-label CIFAR-10 examples, to zero training error.
rows.note: The paper says the larger MLP has a larger η and slower convergence; it does not isolate width from depth or establish a width threshold.
rows.check: MLP8 increases hidden-layer count from two to seven while retaining hidden-layer width. This tests depth, not V2. Slower convergence refers to training-sample requirements, not optimization speed; 40,5M means 40.5 million parameters.

rows.subject: ResNet018
rows.operation_detail: Compared with MLP3 on natural-label CIFAR-10 across a sweep of training-set sizes, with zero training error.
rows.note: The authors state that MLP Emin is much larger than ResNet Emin. This comparison supports lower fitted minimum error for the convolutional model in this setting.
rows.check: The comparison supports V3, but 0.095 versus 0.363 are fitted asymptotic errors, not directly measured test errors at a particular sample count.

relationships.condition: Approximately parameter-matched ResNet018/MLP3 and ResNet101/MLP8 on CIFAR-10, trained from scratch with LAMB without augmentation or weight decay.
relationships.reason: R5–R8 report lower fitted asymptotic errors for ResNets: 0.095 versus 0.363 and 0.067 versus 0.360, consistent with the held-out learning-curve comparisons in Figure 5.
relationships.display_finding: For the first model pair, fitted asymptotic error fractions were 0.095 for ResNet and 0.363 for the MLP. For the second pair, they were 0.067 for ResNet and 0.360 for the MLP.
